label: servo_press_simulation
info:
Simulates Servo Press Modbus §8.4.2 readings and POSTs to EAP-PMS /api/machines/telemetry.
Node-RED host: 192.168.1.113
Edit node 'cfg PMS URL + device' before Deploy (PMS URL, device, spool file).

Alarm codes: faults 101/102/103/104 (NG) and warnings 201/202/305 (part still OK) rotate, so the Alarms tab distribution shows one coloured bar per code.

STORE AND FORWARD
If PMS is unreachable (ECONNREFUSED, timeout, 5xx) the sample is appended to servo_press_spool.csv in the Node-RED user directory instead of being lost.
On the next successful POST the spool is replayed oldest row first, then the CSV is emptied. If PMS drops again mid-replay the remaining rows stay in the file and the next reconnect picks up where it left off.
'replay spool on start' also drains anything left over from a previous Node-RED session.
CSV columns: iso_time, origin, device_name, device_uuid + one column per Modbus tag (raw register values, exactly as posted).

WHERE IS THE CSV?
'report spool location' warns once per session with the exact path, byte count and the hostname/user Node-RED runs as. If that hostname is not the host you are shelled into, the path is inside Node-RED's own filesystem (container, snap, or PrivateTmp) and a host 'ls' will never show it.
GET http://<node-red-host>:1880/servo-press-spool.csv downloads the spool; it answers 404 while nothing is buffered. In a Kubernetes pod port 1880 is usually not reachable from outside, so use 'kubectl port-forward' first, or copy the file with 'kubectl cp <pod>:/var/tmp/servo_press_spool.csv .'.

INSPECT THE SPOOL FROM THE EDITOR (no shell needed)
'spool: summary' -> path, size, row count, oldest and newest sample.
'spool: next 5 rows' -> the next five buffered samples as named fields, one row per debug message (the sidebar truncates at 1000 characters, so packing a page into one message would cut it off). Press again to walk forward; it wraps at the end.
'spool: back to first row' -> reset the paging cursor.
'spool: download URL' -> asks this Node-RED's /settings for httpNodeRoot and prints the exact path to open in a browser, e.g. <httpNodeRoot>/servo-press-spool.csv.

RUNNING IN A POD
The container filesystem is wiped on pod restart, so keep the spool on the mounted volume that holds the Node-RED user directory ('/data' in the official image). The 'probe writable paths' inject reports which directories this container can write to.

simulate Modbus §8.4.2 readings

spool row to CSV

load spooled rows
next spooled row
